title.zh: 卷267 列傳五十四 张玉书 李天馥 吴琠 张英 陈廷敬 温达 萧永藻 嵩祝 王顼龄
title.en: Volume 267 Biographies 54: Zhang Yushu, Li Tianfu, Wu Tian, Zhang Ying, Chen Tingjing, Wen Da, Xiao Yongzao, Song Zhu, Wang Xuling
title.raw: 卷267 列傳五十四 张玉书 李天馥 吴琠 张英 陈廷敬 温达 萧永藻 嵩祝 王顼龄

sentences.zh: 張玉書，字素存，江南丹徒人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yushu, style name Sucun, was a native of Dantu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yushu, whose courtesy name was Sucun, came from Dantu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父九徵，字湘曉。

translations.literal: His father was Jiuzheng, style name Xiangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiuzheng used the courtesy name Xiangxiao.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he took first place in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2, he ranked first in the provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 九年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he passed the metropolitan examination and received the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 博學礪行，精春秋三傳，尤邃於史。

translations.literal: Broad in learning and strict in conduct, he mastered the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals and was especially profound in history.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and upright, he excelled in the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals and was especially deep in historical studies.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部文選郎中。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 出為河南提學僉事，考績最，當超擢，遽引疾歸。

translations.literal: He went out as Educational Commissioner of Henan; his performance review ranked highest and he was due for exceptional promotion, but he abruptly pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Educational Intendant of Henan, he earned the top rating in his review and was slated for rapid promotion, yet he at once cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 玉書，順治十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Yushu became a jinshi in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yushu passed as jinshi in Shunzhi 18, entered the Hanlin Academy as a Bachelor, and received appointment as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷左庶子，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Sub-Reader and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Left Sub-Reader and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，以進講稱旨，加詹事銜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi, because his lectures pleased the Emperor, he was given the additional title of Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 his lectures won the Emperor's approval, and he was granted the additional rank of Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢內閣學士，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician and appointed Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was elevated to Grand Secretariat Academician and made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部侍郎，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Vice Minister of Rites while also serving as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三籓平，有請行封禪者，玉書建議駁之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: When the Three Feudatories were pacified, some petitioned to perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices; Yushu memorialized to reject it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Feudatories rebellion was crushed, some urged the Feng and Shan rites; Zhang Yushu submitted a memorial opposing them, and the proposal lapsed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，丁父憂，上遣內閣學士王鴻緒至邸賜奠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, upon his father's death he entered mourning; the Emperor sent Grand Secretariat Academician Wang Hongxu to his residence to bestow sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23, while mourning his father, he received an imperial gift when Grand Secretariat Academician Wang Hongxu was sent to his home to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 服闋，即家起刑部尚書，調兵部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was summoned from home to Minister of Justice, then transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was called from home to Minister of Justice and then shifted to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，河道總督靳輔奏中河工成。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Grand Canal Director Jin Fu reported that the Middle Canal works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27, Canal Director Jin Fu reported completion of the Middle Canal project.

sentences.zh: 時學士開音布往勘稱善，監高郵石工，疏請閉塞支河口為中河蓄水。

translations.literal: At the time Academician Kaiyebu went to inspect and pronounced it good, supervised the Gaoyou stonework, and memorialized to block the branch river mouth to store water for the Middle Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Kaiyebu inspected the works, approved them, oversaw the Gaoyou stone project, and petitioned to seal the branch outlet to impound water for the Middle Canal.

sentences.zh: 上以於成龍嘗奏輔開中河無益累民，今中河工成，乃命玉書偕尚書圖納等往勘，並遍察毛城鋪、高家堰及海口狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Yu Chenglong had once memorialized that Jin Fu's opening of the Middle Canal was useless and burdened the people, now that the Middle Canal works were done ordered Yushu together with Minister Tuna and others to go inspect, and also to examine thoroughly the conditions at Maochengpu, Gaojiayan, and the estuary.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yu Chenglong had once argued that Jin Fu's Middle Canal would only harm the people, the Emperor now that the canal was finished sent Zhang Yushu with Minister Tuna and others to inspect it and survey Maochengpu, Gaojiayan, and the estuary as well.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上謂玉書曰：「此行當秉公陳奏，毋效熊一瀟託故推諉為也。」

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, the Emperor said to Yushu: "On this mission you must report impartially; do not follow Xiong Yixiao's example of making excuses to shirk responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, the Emperor told Zhang Yushu: "Report fairly on this tour; do not emulate Xiong Yixiao and dodge duty with pretexts."

sentences.zh: 玉書等還奏：「勘閱河形，黃河西岸出水高。

translations.literal: When Yushu and the others returned and memorialized: "Upon inspecting the river course, the water issuing from the west bank of the Yellow River was high.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yushu and his party reported back: "In our inspection of the river, the outflow on the Yellow River's west bank stood high.

sentences.zh: 年來水大，未溢出岸上，知河身並未淤塞。

translations.literal: In recent years the water has been great yet has not overflowed the banks, showing that the river channel is not silted up.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy flows in recent years have not topped the banks, which shows the channel is not choked with silt.

sentences.zh: 海口岸寬二三里，河流入海無所阻。

translations.literal: The estuary banks are two or three li wide, and the river entering the sea meets no obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: At the mouth the shore spans two or three li, and the river meets no barrier as it reaches the sea.

sentences.zh: 中河工成，舟楫往來，免涉黃河一百八十里之險。

translations.literal: With the Middle Canal works completed, boats coming and going are spared the peril of one hundred eighty li on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Middle Canal is finished, traffic avoids the hundred-and-eighty-li hazard of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 但與黃河逼，河寬固不可，狹又不能容運河及駱馬湖之水。

translations.literal: But it lies close to the Yellow River; if the channel is wide that will not do, yet if narrow it cannot hold the waters of the Grand Canal and Luoma Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it hugs the Yellow River: widening it is impossible, while a narrow bed cannot take both Grand Canal water and Luoma Lake overflow.

sentences.zh: 擬請於蕭家渡、楊家莊增建減水壩，相時宣洩。

translations.literal: It is proposed to build additional flood-release dams at Xiaojiadu and Yangjiazhuang to discharge water as conditions require.
translations.idiomatic: We propose new spill dams at Xiaojiadu and Yangjiazhuang to release water when needed.

sentences.zh: 閉塞支河口，應如開音布議。」

translations.literal: Blocking the branch river mouth should follow Kaiyebu's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: Sealing the branch outlet should follow Kaiyebu's recommendation."

sentences.zh: 上悉從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor fully approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted all of this.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫金鋐以民杜光遇陳訴駐防滿洲兵擾民，下布政使李之粹察訊。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Jin Hong reported that the commoner Du Guangyu petitioned that garrison Manchu troops were harassing the people, and the case was referred to Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Zhicui for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Jin Hong forwarded a complaint by Du Guangyu that Manchu garrison troops were molesting civilians, and ordered Provincial Commissioner Li Zhicui to investigate.

sentences.zh: 之粹諮杭州將軍郭丕請申禁，郭丕以聞。

translations.literal: Zhicui consulted Hangzhou General Guo Pi to request a prohibition, and Guo Pi reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhicui asked Hangzhou General Guo Pi to issue a ban, and Guo Pi reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書熊賜履往按，賜履丁憂去，改命玉書。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Minister Xiong Cilu to investigate; Cilu left on mourning, and the order was changed to Yushu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Minister Xiong Cilu to look into the matter; when Cilu withdrew for mourning, Zhang Yushu was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 尋調禮部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上南巡，駐蹕蘇州，玉書還奏杜光遇無其人，所陳訴皆虛妄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, on the southern tour the Emperor halted at Suzhou; Yushu reported back that Du Guangyu did not exist and that the entire petition was false.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28, during the southern tour with the court at Suzhou, Zhang Yushu reported that there was no such person as Du Guangyu and that every allegation was fabricated.

sentences.zh: 金鋐、李之粹皆坐奪官，流徙。

translations.literal: Jin Hong and Li Zhicui were both stripped of office and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Hong and Li Zhicui were both dismissed and banished.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜文華殿大學士，兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and concurrently Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he became Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall while also serving as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，靳輔奏高家堰加築小堤，復命玉書偕圖納往勘。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Jin Fu memorialized to add small dikes at Gaojiayan, and Yushu was again ordered with Tuna to go inspect.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31, Jin Fu proposed supplementary embankments at Gaojiayan, and Zhang Yushu was again sent with Tuna to inspect.

sentences.zh: 還言：「曩者黃漲，淮流被逼，故洪澤湖水視昔為高。

translations.literal: On returning he said: "Formerly when the Yellow rose, the Huai was forced aside, so the waters of Hongze Lake stood higher than before.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "When the Yellow River swelled in the past, it pressed the Huai aside, so Hongze Lake stood higher than it once had.

sentences.zh: 今擬築堤，距高家堰甚近；

translations.literal: Now it is proposed to build dikes very close to Gaojiayan;
translations.idiomatic: The plan now is to build dikes very near Gaojiayan;

sentences.zh: 若水漲，則高家堰大堤且不保，築小堤何益？

translations.literal: if water rises, then even the great dike at Gaojiayan may not be preserved—of what use is building small dikes?
translations.idiomatic: should floods come, even the main Gaojiayan embankment may fail—what good are minor dikes then?

sentences.zh: 因條列高家堰河工，自史家刮至周橋一萬四百馀丈，宜築堤三官廟。

translations.literal: He therefore itemized the Gaojiayan river works from Shijiagua to Zhouqiao, ten thousand four hundred-odd zhang, where dikes should be built at Sanguanmiao.
translations.idiomatic: He listed Gaojiayan works from Shijiagua to Zhouqiao—more than ten thousand four hundred zhang—and urged diking at Sanguanmiao.

sentences.zh: 諸口宜改石工。

translations.literal: The various openings should be converted to stonework.
translations.idiomatic: Every breach should be faced with stone.

sentences.zh: 今擬築小堤處，宜令河臣每歲親勘。」

translations.literal: At the place now proposed for small dikes, the river officials should be ordered to inspect in person each year."
translations.idiomatic: Where small dikes were proposed, canal officers should make annual inspections in person."

sentences.zh: 上深然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，玉書扈行，預參帷幄。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; Yushu accompanied the expedition and took part in council beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 the Emperor led a campaign against Galdan; Zhang Yushu followed the court and joined pre-battle planning.

sentences.zh: 師次克魯倫河，噶爾丹北竄，大將軍費揚古截擊，斬殺幾盡，噶爾丹僅以身免。

translations.literal: When the army halted at the Kerulen River, Galdan fled north; General-in-Chief Fiyanggū intercepted and killed nearly all; Galdan escaped only with his life.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kerulen the army halted; Galdan fled north, but Field Marshal Fiyanggū cut him off and slaughtered nearly his entire force, leaving Galdan to flee alone.

sentences.zh: 玉書率百官上賀。

translations.literal: Yushu led the hundred officials in offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yushu led the civil and military officials in presenting congratulations.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，充平定朔漠方略總裁官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Pacification of the Northern Deserts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 he was appointed chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Pacification of the Northern Deserts.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，遣官賜祭，並賜御書松廕堂榜。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death, officials were sent to offer sacrifice, and he was also granted an imperial inscription for the hall name Songyin Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the court sent officers to sacrifice and bestowed an imperial plaque reading Songyin Tang.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，玉書迎謁，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, on the southern tour Yushu came out to welcome and attend; rewards were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38, during the southern tour, Zhang Yushu came forward to welcome the Emperor and received added gifts.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，服未闋，召至京，入閣視事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, before mourning had ended he was summoned to the capital to enter the Grand Council and handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39, though mourning was unfinished, he was called to Beijing to join the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 四十年，扈駕南巡，駐蹕江寧，召試士子，命為閱卷官。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, he accompanied the southern tour; the court halted at Jiangning, summoned candidates for examination, and appointed him examiner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he followed the southern tour; at Jiangning the Emperor tested scholars and named Zhang Yushu chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 御舟次高資港，玉書奏言前去鎮江不遠，請幸江天寺，留駐數日，上為留一日。

translations.literal: When the imperial boat reached Gaozigang, Yushu memorialized that Zhenjiang lay not far ahead and requested a visit to Jiangtian Temple and a stay of several days; the Emperor stayed one day.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozigang Zhang Yushu noted that Zhenjiang was near and asked the Emperor to visit Jiangtian Temple and remain several days; the Emperor stayed one day.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，河道總督張鵬翮請開溜淮套河，上南巡，次清口勘視，見所樹標竿多在民塚，召鵬翮極斥其非。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, Canal Director Zhang Penghe requested to open the Liuhuaitao River; on the southern tour the Emperor halted at Qingkou to inspect and saw that most of the stakes marked lay in commoners' graves, and summoned Penghe to rebuke him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 46, Canal Director Zhang Penghe proposed opening the Liuhuaitao channel; on the southern tour at Qingkou the Emperor found survey stakes driven through villagers' tombs and summoned Penghe for a severe reprimand.

sentences.zh: 玉書奏曰：「向者老人白英議引汶水南北分流，不若別作壩引汶水通漕，其下流專以淮水敵黃。

translations.literal: Yushu memorialized: "Formerly the elder Bai Ying proposed diverting the Wen north and south; it would be better to build a separate dam to draw Wen water for the grain transport, and below let the Huai alone contend with the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yushu argued: "Bai Ying once urged splitting the Wen north and south; better to build a separate dam to feed the canal from the Wen and let the Huai alone hold back the Yellow below.

sentences.zh: 黃水趨海，此萬世利也。」

translations.literal: With Yellow water hastening to the sea, this is a benefit for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Driving Yellow River water to the sea would profit posterity forever."

sentences.zh: 上善其言，遂諭鵬翮罷開溜淮套，事具鵬翮傳。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and thereupon ordered Penghe to abandon opening the Liuhuaitao; the matter is given in full in Penghe's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised this and ordered Penghe to drop the Liuhuaitao project, as related in Penghe's biography.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，以疾乞休，溫旨慰留。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, he begged leave on account of illness; a warm edict urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 49 he asked to retire for illness; the Emperor sent a gracious edict asking him to stay.

sentences.zh: 五十年，從幸熱河，甫至疾作，遂卒，年七十，上深惜之，親制輓詩，賜白金千。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, following the tour to Rehe, he had just arrived when illness seized him and he died at age seventy; the Emperor deeply regretted it, composed an elegy in his own hand, and granted one thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In year 50, on the Rehe tour, he fell ill as soon as he arrived and died at seventy; the Emperor mourned deeply, wrote an elegy himself, and gave a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 命內務府監製棺槨衾絞，驛送其喪還京師，加贈太子太保，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He ordered the Imperial Household Department to supervise making coffin, shroud, and pall, had the bier escorted by post relay to the capital, posthumously promoted him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household was ordered to furnish coffin and shroud, his body was relayed to Beijing, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and honored with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，上追念舊勞，擢其子編修逸少為侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, recalling his old service, the Emperor promoted his son, Compiler Yishao, to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In year 52, remembering his long service, the Emperor promoted his son Compiler Yishao to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 玉書謹慎廉潔，居政地二十年，遠避權勢，門無雜賓，從容密勿，為聖祖所親任。

translations.literal: Yushu was cautious, incorrupt, and clean; for twenty years in high office he kept far from power, his gate admitted no mixed guests, and with calm discretion he was intimately trusted by the Kangxi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yushu was prudent and scrupulously honest; twenty years at the summit of government he shunned faction, kept no dubious visitors, and with steady counsel won the Kangxi Emperor's deep trust.

sentences.zh: 自奉儉約，飲食服禦，略如寒素。

translations.literal: In his own conduct he was frugal; food, drink, and dress were nearly those of a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly himself—meals and dress scarcely above a scholar in want.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he entered the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he was enshrined in the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.

sentences.zh: 李天馥，字湘北，河南永城人。

translations.literal: Li Tianfu, style name Xiangbei, was a native of Yongcheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tianfu, courtesy name Xiangbei, was from Yongcheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 先世在明初以軍功得世襲廬州衛指揮僉事，家合肥。

translations.literal: His forebears in the early Ming received by military merit a hereditary post as Assistant Commander of the Luzhou Guard, and the family dwelt in Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor in early Ming earned by military merit the hereditary post of Assistant Commander of the Luzhou Guard; the family lived in Hefei.

sentences.zh: 有族子佔永城衛籍，天馥以其籍舉鄉試。

translations.literal: A clansman held registration in the Yongcheng Guard, and Tianfu used that registration to take the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman held Yongcheng Guard household registration, which Tianfu used to sit for the provincial exam.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he passed as jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a Bachelor, and was made Reviser.

sentences.zh: 博聞約取，究心經世之學，名藉甚。

translations.literal: Broad in learning yet selective in taking, he devoted himself to statecraft; his fame was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Learned yet discriminating, he devoted himself to practical statecraft and enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat Academician and served as Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Secretariat Academician and lectured at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 每侍直，有所見，悉陳無隱，聖祖器之，康熙十九年夏，旱，命偕大學士明珠會三法司慮囚，有矜疑者，悉從末減。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended on duty and had observations, he stated them all without concealment; the Kangxi Emperor valued him. In the summer of the nineteenth year of Kangxi, during drought, he was ordered together with Grand Secretary Mingzhu to join the Three Judicial Offices in reviewing prisoners; where there was doubt, all were reduced to the lesser penalty.
translations.idiomatic: On duty he spoke his mind without reserve and won the Emperor's esteem. In the drought summer of Kangxi 19 he joined Grand Secretary Mingzhu and the Three Judicial Offices to review prisoners, commuting every doubtful case to a lighter sentence.

sentences.zh: 尋擢戶部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, then transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of Revenue, then moved to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 杜絕苞苴，嚴峻一無所私，銓政稱平。

translations.literal: He cut off bribery entirely, was stern and admitted no private favor, and appointments were called fair.
translations.idiomatic: He refused all gifts, brooked no favoritism, and his appointments won a reputation for fairness.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 河道總督靳輔議築高家堰重堤，束水出清口，停濬海口；

translations.literal: Canal Director Jin Fu proposed building a heavy dike at Gaojiayan to confine water out of Qingkou and suspend dredging the estuary;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu urged a massive Gaojiayan embankment to force water through Qingkou and halt estuary dredging;

sentences.zh: 於成龍主疏濬下河。

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong advocated dredging the lower river.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong favored dredging the lower reach.

sentences.zh: 上召二人詣京師入對，仍各持一說，下廷臣詳議，天馥謂下河海口當濬，高家堰重堤宜停築，上然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the two to the capital to answer in person; each still held to one view, and the matter was referred to the court for detailed discussion. Tianfu said the lower river and estuary should be dredged and the heavy dike at Gaojiayan should be halted; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both were called to Beijing to debate; still at odds, the case went to the full court. Tianfu argued for dredging the lower river and mouth and against Jin Fu's heavy dike; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 歷刑、兵、吏諸部。

translations.literal: He passed through the ministries of Justice, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn at Justice, War, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，拜武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 he was made Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「機務重任，不可用喜事人。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The weight of state affairs cannot be given to men who love novelty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Critical duties must not go to men who court novelty.

sentences.zh: 天馥老成清慎，學行俱優，朕知其必不生事。」

translations.literal: Tianfu is seasoned, pure, and cautious; in learning and conduct he is both excellent—I know he will certainly not make trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu is mature, upright, and careful, excellent in learning and conduct—I know he will never stir trouble."

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以母憂回籍，上賜「貞松」榜御書，勉以儒者之學；

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, on his mother's mourning he returned home; the Emperor granted the imperial inscription "Chaste Pine" and exhorted him in the way of the Confucian scholar;
translations.idiomatic: In year 32, mourning his mother, he went home; the Emperor gave him the plaque "Chaste Pine" and urged Confucian self-cultivation;

sentences.zh: 复謂：「天馥侍朕三十馀年，未嘗有失。

translations.literal: he also said: "Tianfu has attended me for more than thirty years and has never once been at fault.
translations.idiomatic: adding: "Tianfu has served me over thirty years without a single lapse.

sentences.zh: 三年易過，命懸缺以待。」

translations.literal: Three years pass quickly—order that the vacancy be held for him."
translations.idiomatic: Three years pass quickly—keep his seat open until he returns."

sentences.zh: 三十四年，服將闋，起故官，入閣視事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, as mourning was about to end, he was restored to his former post and entered the Grand Council to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34, as mourning neared its end, he resumed his old post and rejoined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 上親征厄魯特，平定朔漠，兵革甫息，天馥務以清靜和平，與民休息。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally campaigned against the Eleuths and pacified the northern deserts; as arms had just ceased, Tianfu strove for quiet and peace so the people could rest.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor's campaigns against the Eleuths and pacification of the north, Tianfu pressed for calm so the people could recover.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「變法不如守法。

translations.literal: He once said: "Changing the law is not as good as keeping the law.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Reforming statutes is worse than upholding them.

sentences.zh: 奉行成憲，不失尺寸，乃所以報也。」

translations.literal: Upholding established statutes without losing a fraction of measure—that is how one repays one's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Following the code to the inch—that is how one discharges one's debt to the throne."

sentences.zh: 三十八年，卒，諡文定。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he died; his posthumous title was Wending.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 he died and received the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 天馥在位，留意人才，嘗應詔舉彭鵬、陸隴其、邵嗣堯，卒為名臣。

translations.literal: While in office Tianfu paid attention to talent; he once responded to an imperial call to recommend Peng Peng, Lu Longqi, and Shao Siyao, who all became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In office he cultivated talent; answering an imperial summons he recommended Peng Peng, Lu Longqi, and Shao Siyao, each later a noted minister.

sentences.zh: 為學士時，冬月慮囚，有知縣李方廣坐當死，天馥言其有才，得緩決，尋以赦免。

translations.literal: When he was Academician, in winter he reviewed prisoners; a magistrate Li Fanguang was sentenced to death, and Tianfu said he had talent and obtained a stay of execution; soon he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician, reviewing winter prisoners, he spared magistrate Li Fanguang, whom he called talented though condemned to death; Li was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 刑部囚多瘐斃，為庀屋材，多為之所，別罪之輕重以居，活者尤眾。

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Justice many prisoners died of illness in confinement; he supplied timber for buildings and made many places for them, separating light and heavy offenses in residence, and those who lived were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At Justice many inmates died of jail fever; he procured timber, built more wards, and sorted prisoners by severity, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 事親孝，居喪廬墓，有雙白燕飛至，不去，人名其居為白燕廬。

translations.literal: Filial in serving his parents, in mourning he dwelt at the tomb; a pair of white swallows flew there and would not leave, and people named his dwelling White Swallow Hut.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to his parents, he mourned at the grave; two white swallows came and would not leave, and people called his lodge White Swallow Hut.

sentences.zh: 子孚青，進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Fuzing was a jinshi and served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuzing was a jinshi and held the post of Compiler.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸，不復出。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home and never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he went home and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 吳琠，字伯美，山西沁州人。

translations.literal: Wu Tian, style name Bomei, was a native of Qinzhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tian, courtesy name Bomei, was from Qinzhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年進士，授河南確山知縣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Queshan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 he passed as jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Queshan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 縣遭明季流寇殘破，琠拊流亡，闢蕪廢，墾田歲增，捕獲盜魁誅之。

translations.literal: The county had been ravaged by bandits of the late Ming; Tian comforted the displaced, opened abandoned fields, and year by year reclaimed land increased; he captured and executed the ringleaders of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay in ruins from late-Ming rebels; Wu Tian resettled refugees, reopened wasteland, and yearly acreage grew; he seized and executed bandit chiefs.

sentences.zh: 師下雲南，縣當孔道，輿馬糧餉，先事籌辦而民不擾。

translations.literal: When the army marched on Yunnan, the county lay on the main route; carts, horses, grain, and fodder were prepared beforehand yet the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When troops advanced on Yunnan the county sat on the supply route; he prepared transport and provisions ahead of time without troubling the people.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，以卓異入為吏部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, for outstanding performance he entered the capital as a Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and rose through the ranks to Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, rated outstanding, he entered Beijing as a Principal Clerk in Personnel and rose to Director.

sentences.zh: 累遷通政司右參議。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書魏象樞亟稱其賢。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Wei Xiangqi repeatedly praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Wei Xiangqi often commended his ability.

sentences.zh: 二十年，特擢右通政，累遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was specially promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission and in succession to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was specially promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission, then rose to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏請復督撫巡方，略言：「令甲，督撫於命下之日，即杜門屏客；

translations.literal: He memorialized to restore governors-general and governors' tours of the regions, saying in summary: "By regulation, from the day the order is issued governors-general and governors must shut their gates and screen visitors;
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to restore provincial tours, writing in part: "Regulations require that from the day of appointment governors-general and governors shut their gates to callers;

sentences.zh: 蒞任，守令不得參謁。

translations.literal: on taking office, prefects and magistrates may not pay calls.
translations.idiomatic: once in post, prefects and magistrates may not present themselves.

sentences.zh: 凡有舉劾，惟據道府揭報，愛憎毀譽，真偽相亂，督撫無由知。

translations.literal: For all recommendations and impeachments they rely only on reports from circuit and prefectural officials; love, hatred, praise, and blame, truth and falsehood are mixed together, and governors have no way to know.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions and impeachments rest solely on circuit and prefectural memorials, where favor and slander mingle truth with lies beyond a governor's ken.

sentences.zh: 革火耗而火耗愈甚，禁私派而私派愈增。

translations.literal: Abolish meltage fees and meltage grows worse; forbid private levies and private levies increase.
translations.idiomatic: Banning meltage fees only made them heavier; forbidding unauthorized surcharges only swelled them.

sentences.zh: 請敕督撫親歷各屬，以知守令賢否。

translations.literal: Request an edict that governors-general and governors personally tour each subordinate to learn whether prefects and magistrates are worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors-general and governors tour their jurisdictions in person to judge local officials.

sentences.zh: 或謂巡方恐勞擾百姓，夫督撫賢，則必能禁迎送、卻供應；

translations.literal: Some say touring the regions will harass the people; if governors are worthy, they can surely forbid welcoming parties and refuse supplies;
translations.idiomatic: Critics feared tours would burden the people; but worthy governors can forbid lavish welcomes and refuse gifts;

sentences.zh: 如其不肖，雖端坐會城，而暮夜之餽踵至，豈獨巡方足以勞民哉？」

translations.literal: if they are unworthy, even sitting at the provincial capital, night gifts still arrive in succession—is touring alone what burdens the people?"
translations.idiomatic: unworthy ones, though they never leave the capital, still receive nightly bribes—is touring alone what harms the people?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「巡撫及巡守道無一旅之衛，而提鎮各建高牙。

translations.literal: He also said: "Governors and touring surveillance commissioners have not a single company of guards, while provincial commanders each raise lofty banners.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Governors and surveillance commissioners lack even a company of guards, while regional commanders maintain grand headquarters.

sentences.zh: 前撫臣如馬雄鎮，道臣如陳啟泰，懷忠秉義，向使各有兵馬，奚至束手？

translations.literal: Former governors such as Ma Xiongzhen and surveillance commissioners such as Chen Qitai cherished loyalty and upheld righteousness; had each possessed troops, how could they have been left helpless?
translations.idiomatic: Governors like Ma Xiongzhen and commissioners like Chen Qitai were loyal and upright; with troops of their own they need not have been helpless.

sentences.zh: 宜及此時復舊制，使巡撫、巡守道仍各管兵馬。

translations.literal: It is fitting at this time to restore the old system and let governors and touring surveillance commissioners again each command troops.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring the old system so governors and surveillance commissioners again commanded troops.

sentences.zh: 減提督，增總兵，以一鎮之兵酌分數鎮，聽督撫節制。」

translations.literal: Reduce provincial commanders, increase regional commanders, apportion one command's troops among several commands, and let governors-general and governors control them."
translations.idiomatic: Cut provincial commanders, add regional commanders, divide one command's forces among several posts, and place them under governors' control."

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷兵部侍郎，尋授湖廣巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of War, and soon appointed Governor of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he became Vice Minister of War, then Governor of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 湖北自裁兵亂後，奸猾率指仇人為亂黨，株連不已，琠悉置不問，而懲其妄訐者，人心大定。

translations.literal: After the reduction of troops in Hubei, the cunning often denounced enemies as rebels; implicated persons mounted without end. Tian ignored them all and punished those who falsely accused, and popular sentiment was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: After troop cuts in Hubei, schemers denounced rivals as rebels in endless chains; Wu Tian dismissed such cases and punished false accusers, greatly calming the province.

sentences.zh: 陝西飢，流民入湖廣就食，令有司分賑，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered famine and refugees entered Huguang to find food; he ordered officials to distribute relief by districts, and very many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi starved, refugees streamed into Huguang; he ordered district relief and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，詔以荊州兵船運漕米十萬石至襄陽備賑，琠議：「兵船泊大江下至漢口受米，復西上抵襄陽，計程二千馀裡。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, an edict ordered Jingzhou military boats to transport one hundred thousand shi of grain tribute to Xiangyang for relief; Tian proposed: "Military boats moor on the great river down to Hankou to receive grain, then go up west to Xiangyang—a course of more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 the court ordered Jingzhou war junks to carry a hundred thousand shi of tribute grain to Xiangyang for famine relief; Wu Tian argued: "War boats must sail the Yangtze to Hankou, then west to Xiangyang—over two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 令原運漕船若乘夏水順道赴襄陽，僅七百馀裡，即以便宜行事。」

translations.literal: Let the original grain-transport boats, if they catch the summer flood and go directly to Xiangyang, travel only seven hundred-odd li, and act on this expedient basis."
translations.idiomatic: Let the regular tribute fleet use summer floods straight to Xiangyang—only seven hundred-odd li—and act on that expedient."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嘉之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised the memorial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁母憂，服未闋，即授湖廣總督，仍聽終制乃赴任。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother; before mourning ended he was appointed Governor-General of Huguang and was still allowed to finish mourning before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon mourning his mother; though mourning was unfinished he was named Governor-General of Huguang but allowed to complete mourning first.

sentences.zh: 故事，土司見州縣吏不敢抗禮，其後大吏稍稍假借之。

translations.literal: By precedent, native chieftains when meeting prefectural and county officials did not dare refuse obeisance; afterward high officials gradually lent them precedence.
translations.idiomatic: By custom native chieftains bowed to county officials; later senior officers gradually indulged them.

sentences.zh: 琠至，絕餽遺，飭謁見長吏悉循舊制，或犯約束，檄諭之，無敢肆者。

translations.literal: When Tian arrived, he cut off gifts entirely and ordered audiences with superior officials to follow the old system; if any violated the rules, he issued a proclamation, and none dared act recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tian refused all gifts and required chieftains to observe old protocol with superiors; violators were warned by edict and none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，召為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he was summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 he was recalled as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 he served as chief metropolitan examiner.

sentences.zh: 上北征回鑾，顧迎駕諸臣，褒琠及河道總督張鵬翮居官之廉，即擢琠為刑部尚書，而以鵬翮為左都御史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from the northern campaign and looked at those who welcomed him, he praised Tian and Canal Director Zhang Penghe for integrity in office and at once promoted Tian to Minister of Justice and Penghe to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from campaign, the Emperor praised Wu Tian and Zhang Penghe for clean government, promoting Tian to Minister of Justice and Penghe to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，拜保和殿大學士，兼刑部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Baohe Hall and concurrently Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 37 he became Grand Secretary of the Baohe Hall while retaining the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 琠熟諳舊章，參決庶務，靡不允當。

translations.literal: Tian was thoroughly versed in old regulations; in deciding routine affairs nothing failed to be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in old regulations, his judgments on routine business were invariably sound.

sentences.zh: 奏對皆竭忱悃，上每稱善。

translations.literal: In memorial audiences he spoke with full sincerity; the Emperor often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he spoke with complete candor, which the Emperor often commended.

sentences.zh: 所薦引多賢能吏。

translations.literal: Those he recommended and introduced were mostly able officials.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his recommendations proved able men.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，复典會試，上手書「風度端凝」榜賜之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, he again presided over the metropolitan examination; the Emperor wrote in his own hand the plaque "Demeanor dignified and composed" and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 he again ran the metropolitan exam; the Emperor wrote and gave him the plaque "Demeanor dignified and composed."

sentences.zh: 尋具疏乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized in full to beg retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned to retire; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 上嘗臨米芾書以賜琠，書其后曰：「吳琠寬厚和平，持己清廉。

translations.literal: The Emperor once brought out Mi Fu's calligraphy to give Tian and wrote after it: "Wu Tian is generous, mild, and peaceful, holding himself with clean integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once gifted him Mi Fu's calligraphy and inscribed: "Wu Tian is generous and mild, upright and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 先任封疆，軍民受其實惠。

translations.literal: In his former posts on the frontier, soldiers and people received real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he had brought real benefit to soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 朝中之事，面折廷諍，能得其正。

translations.literal: In court affairs he spoke frankly in debate and could obtain what was right.
translations.idiomatic: At court he debated frankly and hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 朕甚重其能得大臣之體。」

translations.literal: I greatly value that he possesses the bearing of a great minister."
translations.idiomatic: I greatly esteem his bearing as a great minister."

sentences.zh: 四十四年，卒，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he died; his posthumous title was Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 he died and received the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 翰林院撰祭文，上以為未能盡琠，敕改撰。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy drafted the funerary text; the Emperor thought it did not fully capture Tian and ordered it rewritten.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin's elegy failed to satisfy the Emperor, who ordered a rewrite.

sentences.zh: 吏部奏大學士缺員，上以琠喪未歸，懸缺未即別除，曰：「朕心不忍也。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel reported a vacancy among Grand Secretaries; because Tian's funeral had not returned, the vacancy was held and no immediate replacement made; the Emperor said: "My heart cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Personnel reported a Grand Secretary vacancy; with Tian's body not yet home the post was left open; the Emperor said: "My heart cannot bear to fill it yet."

sentences.zh: 琠所至多惠政，兩湖及確山皆祠祀。

translations.literal: Wherever Tian served there were many benevolent policies; both Huguang and Queshan enshrined him in temples.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left benevolent rule; Huguang and Queshan both erected temples to him.

sentences.zh: 初，沁州薦飢，琠糴米賑之，全活無算。

translations.literal: At first, when Qinzhou suffered famine, Tian purchased rice for relief and preserved lives beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzhou first suffered famine he bought rice for relief and saved untold lives.

sentences.zh: 有司議增沁糧一千三百石，琠力爭乃已。

translations.literal: Officials proposed increasing Qinzhou grain quota by one thousand three hundred shi; Tian strove against it and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wanted to add thirteen hundred shi to Qinzhou's grain quota; Wu Tian fought the measure off.

sentences.zh: 鄉人德之，立祠以祀。

translations.literal: The people of his district were grateful and erected a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: His countrymen in gratitude built a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he entered the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he was enshrined in the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.

sentences.zh: 張英，字敦复，江南桐城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, style name Dunfu, was a native of Tongcheng in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying, courtesy name Dunfu, came from Tongcheng in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he passed as jinshi and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，服闋，授編修，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home; when mourning ended he was appointed Compiler and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he returned to service as Compiler and Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 十六年，聖祖命擇詞臣諄謹有學者日侍左右，設南書房。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Kangxi Emperor ordered selection of literary officials who were earnest, cautious, and learned to attend daily at his side, and established the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 the Emperor chose earnest, learned literary officials for daily attendance and founded the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 命英入直，賜第西安門內。

translations.literal: Ying was ordered to enter on duty and granted a residence inside Xi'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying entered on duty and received a house inside Xi'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 詞臣賜居禁城自此始。

translations.literal: Literary officials granted residence within the Forbidden City began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Court writers living inside the Forbidden City began with him.

sentences.zh: 時方討三籓，軍書旁午，上日禦乾清門聽政後，即幸懋勤殿，與儒臣講論經義。

translations.literal: At the time the Three Feudatories were being suppressed and military documents poured in; after daily audience at the Gate of Heavenly Purity the Emperor would go to the Hall of Exertion in Culture to discuss the classics with Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: While the Three Feudatories were being crushed, the Emperor after morning audience at Qianqing Gate went to Maqin Hall to discuss classics with scholars.

sentences.zh: 英率辰入暮出，退或復宣召，輟食趨宮門，慎密恪勤，上益器之。

translations.literal: Ying entered at dawn and left at dusk; sometimes after retiring he was summoned again, abandoning meals to hurry to the palace gate—careful, secret, and diligent—and the Emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying came at dawn and left at dusk, sometimes recalled after hours, skipping meals to reach the gate—discreet and tireless—and won deeper favor.

sentences.zh: 幸南苑及巡行四方，必以英從。

translations.literal: On tours of the Southern Park and journeys in all directions, Ying was always made to follow.
translations.idiomatic: On southern park outings and travels everywhere, Zhang Ying always accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 一時制誥，多出其手。

translations.literal: Imperial edicts of the time mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Many imperial proclamations of the day bore his pen.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林院學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academy Chancellor and concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hanlin Chancellor and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以葬父乞假，優詔允之，賜白金五百、表裡緞二十，予其父秉彝卹典視英官。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, begging leave to bury his father, he received a gracious edict of approval and was granted five hundred taels of silver and twenty bolts of satin, with funeral honors for his father Bingyi equal to Ying's rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, seeking leave to bury his father, he received gracious approval, five hundred taels, twenty bolts of satin, and funeral honors for his father Bingyi matching his own rank.

sentences.zh: 英歸，築室龍眠山中，居四年，起故官。

translations.literal: Ying returned and built a house in the Longmian mountains, dwelling four years, then was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He built a lodge in the Longmian hills, stayed four years, then resumed office.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎，調禮部，兼管詹事府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War, then Rites, and concurrently supervised the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to War, then Rites, while supervising the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 充經筵講官，奏進孝經衍義，命刊布。

translations.literal: He served as Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and memorialized the Extended Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety, which the Emperor ordered published.
translations.idiomatic: As Classics Colloquium lecturer he submitted the Extended Meaning of the Filial Classic for publication.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢工部尚書，兼翰林院掌院學士，仍管詹事府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was promoted to Minister of Works and concurrently Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, still supervising the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he became Minister of Works and Hanlin Chancellor, still overseeing the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 調禮部，兼官如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Rites with concurrent posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Rites while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 編修楊瑄撰都統、一等公佟國綱祭文失辭，坐奪官流徙；

translations.literal: Compiler Yang Xuan composed a funerary text for Commandery Commander and First-rank Duke Tong Guogang with improper wording and was stripped of office and exiled;
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Yang Xuan's elegy for Commandery Commander First-rank Duke Tong Guogang used faulty wording; he was dismissed and banished;

sentences.zh: 斥英不詳審，罷尚書，仍管翰林院、詹事府，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: Ying was rebuked for not reviewing carefully, removed as Minister, but still supervised the Hanlin Academy, Directorate of Education, and instructed Hanlin Bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying was faulted for lax review, stripped of his ministry, but kept Hanlin, the Directorate, and tutoring bachelors.

sentences.zh: 尋复官，充國史、一統志、淵鑑類函、政治典訓、平定朔漠方略總裁官。

translations.literal: Soon his office was restored; he served as chief compiler of the National History, Comprehensive Gazetteer, Mirror of History, Political Institutions, and Veritable Records of the Pacification of the Northern Deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reinstated, he headed compilations of the National History, Gazetteer, historical mirror, political institutions, and northern campaign records.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 he ran the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Soon he begged leave on account of illness; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire for illness; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，拜文華殿大學士，兼禮部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 he became Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 英性和易，不務表襮，有所薦舉，終不使其人知。

translations.literal: Ying's nature was easy and mild; he did not pursue display; when he had recommendations, he never let the person know.
translations.idiomatic: Easy in temperament and free of ostentation, he never told those he recommended.

sentences.zh: 所居無赫赫名。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt he had no resounding fame.
translations.idiomatic: He made no show of renown.

sentences.zh: 在講筵，民生利病，四方水旱，知無不言。

translations.literal: At the lecture seat, on people's livelihood and profit and loss, and floods and droughts in all quarters, he spoke whenever he knew.
translations.idiomatic: At the lecture seat he spoke on livelihood, public welfare, and drought and flood wherever he knew of them.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘗語執政：「張英始終敬慎，有古大臣風。」

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor once told those in power: "Zhang Ying from beginning to end is reverent and cautious, with the manner of an ancient great minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor told his ministers: "Zhang Ying has always been reverent and cautious, with the air of a statesman of old."

sentences.zh: 四十年，以衰病求罷，詔許致仕。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, on account of decline and illness he sought dismissal; an edict permitted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40, aged and ill, he sought release; retirement was granted.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，賜宴暢春園，敕部馳驛如製。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, he was given a banquet at the Garden of Exuberant Spring and the ministries were ordered to provide post relays as for an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he was feasted at Changchun Garden and given relay transport by decree.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上南巡，英迎駕淮安，賜御書榜額、白金千。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, on the southern tour Ying welcomed the court at Huai'an and was granted an imperial plaque and one thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44, on the southern tour, he welcomed the Emperor at Huai'an and received an imperial plaque and a thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 隨至江寧，上將旋蹕，以英懇奏，允留一日。

translations.literal: Following to Jiangning, as the Emperor was about to turn back, because Ying pleaded earnestly, one day's stay was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He followed to Jiangning; as the Emperor prepared to return, Zhang Ying's earnest plea won one more day.

sentences.zh: 時總督阿山欲加錢糧耗銀供南巡費，江寧知府陳鵬年持不可，阿山怒鵬年，欲因是罪之，供張故不辦；

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General Ashan wished to add meltage silver to grain taxes for southern tour expenses; Jiangning Prefect Chen Pengnian held that it could not be done; Ashan hated Pengnian and wished to punish him through this, so supplies were deliberately not prepared;
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ashan wanted extra meltage on grain tax for tour costs; Prefect Chen Pengnian refused; Ashan meant to ruin him and left supplies unprepared;

sentences.zh: 左右又中以蜚語，禍將不測。

translations.literal: those about the Emperor also slandered him with rumors, and disaster was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: court slander nearly destroyed Pengnian.

sentences.zh: 及英入見，上問江南廉吏，首舉鵬年，阿山意為沮，鵬年以是受知於上為名臣。

translations.literal: When Ying had audience, the Emperor asked about honest officials in Jiangnan; Ying first named Pengnian; Ashan's intent was thwarted, and Pengnian thereby won the Emperor's notice and became a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the Emperor asked for honest Jiangnan officials; Zhang Ying named Pengnian first; Ashan's plot failed and Pengnian became a famed minister.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上复南巡，英迎駕清江浦，仍隨至江寧，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, the Emperor again toured south; Ying welcomed him at Qingjiangpu and still followed to Jiangning, with increased rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In year 46, on another southern tour, Zhang Ying met him at Qingjiangpu, followed to Jiangning, and received added gifts.

sentences.zh: 英自壯歲即有田園之思，致政後，優游林下者七年。

translations.literal: From his youth Ying had thoughts of fields and gardens; after leaving office he wandered leisurely among forests and streams for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he longed for country life; after retirement he spent seven peaceful years in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 為聰訓齋語、恆產瑣言，以務本力田、隨分知足誥誡子弟。

translations.literal: He wrote Instructions of the Congxun Studio and Trivial Words on Fixed Property, admonishing sons and younger brothers to attend to fundamentals, work the fields, and be content within their means.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Congxun Studio Sayings and Trivial Words on Fixed Property, urging sons and brothers to farm, keep to essentials, and know contentment.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, he died; his posthumous title was Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 47 he died and received the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 世宗讀書乾清宮，英嘗侍講經書，及即位，追念舊學，贈太子太傅，賜御書榜額揭諸祠宇。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor read books in the Palace of Heavenly Purity; Ying had once lectured on the classics there; when he took the throne, recalling old studies, he posthumously made Ying Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted an imperial plaque for his shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng had studied in Qianqing Palace where Zhang Ying once lectured; on accession he posthumously made him Grand Tutor and gave an imperial plaque for his temple.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng he entered the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 he entered the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，加贈太傅。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor took the throne, he was further posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong ascended, he was further posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子廷瓚，字卣臣。

translations.literal: His son Tingzan, style name Youchen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingzan used the courtesy name Youchen.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年進士，自編修累官少詹事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi; from Compiler he rose in succession to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi 18, he rose from Compiler to Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 先英卒。

translations.literal: He died before Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He predeceased his father.

sentences.zh: 廷玉，自有傳。

translations.literal: Tingyu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 廷璐，字寶臣。

translations.literal: Tinglu, style name Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglu used the courtesy name Baochen.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年，殿試一甲第二名進士，授編修，直南書房，遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, in the palace examination he took second place among the first rank of three and became a jinshi; he was appointed Compiler, entered the Southern Study, and was transferred to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 57 he placed second in the top tier of the palace exam, became Compiler, served in the Southern Study, and rose to Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，督學河南，坐事奪職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, as Educational Commissioner of Henan, he was stripped of office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1, as Henan Educational Commissioner, he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋起侍講，遷詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as Lecturer and transferred to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored as Lecturer, then Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 兩督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: Twice he served as Educational Commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as Jiangsu Educational Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 武進劉綸、長洲沈德潛皆出其門，並致通顯，有名於時。

translations.literal: Liu Lun of Wujin and Shen Deqian of Changzhou were both his students and all reached high office, famous in their time.
translations.idiomatic: His pupils Liu Lun of Wujin and Shen Deqian of Changzhou both rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 進禮部侍郎，予告歸，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, granted leave to return home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, he retired home and died.

sentences.zh: 廷瑑，字桓臣。

translations.literal: Tingzhuan, style name Huanchen.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhuan used the courtesy name Huanchen.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士，自編修累官工部侍郎，充日講官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he became a jinshi; from Compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Works and served as Daily Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: A Yongzheng 1 jinshi, he rose from Compiler to Vice Minister of Works and Daily Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 起居注初無條例，廷瑑彖編載詳贍得體。

translations.literal: At first the Record of the Emperor's Movements had no regulations; Tingzhuan compiled and edited it in full detail with proper form.
translations.idiomatic: When the Record of the Emperor's Movements lacked rules, Tingzhuan compiled it in thorough, proper form.

sentences.zh: 既擢侍郎，兼職如故。

translations.literal: Once promoted to Vice Minister, his concurrent posts were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister, he kept his other posts.

sentences.zh: 終清世，已出翰林而仍職記註者惟廷瑑。

translations.literal: Through the entire Qing, the only one who had left the Hanlin yet still held the post of Recorder was Tingzhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Qing dynasty, Tingzhuan alone among those who had left the Hanlin still held the Recordership.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年，改補內閣學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, he was transferred to Grand Secretariat Academician and concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 9 he became Grand Secretariat Academician and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 典試江西，移疾歸。

translations.literal: He presided over the Jiangxi examination and returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the Jiangxi provincial exam, then retired for illness.

sentences.zh: 廷瑑彖性誠篤，細微必慎。

translations.literal: Tingzhuan by nature was sincere and earnest, careful in the smallest matters.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Tingzhuan was sincere and meticulous in every detail.

sentences.zh: 既歸，刻苦礪行，耿介不妄取。

translations.literal: After returning home, he disciplined himself severely in conduct, upright and not taking what was not his.
translations.idiomatic: At home he disciplined himself rigorously, upright and accepting nothing unearned.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, he died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 he died at eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 上聞，顧左右曰：「張廷瑑兄弟皆舊臣賢者，今盡矣！

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he turned to those about him and said: "The Tingzhuan brothers of the Zhang family were all worthy old ministers—now they are gone!
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news the Emperor told his attendants: "The Zhang Tingzhuan brothers were worthy old servants—all gone now!

sentences.zh: 安可得也？」

translations.literal: How can such men be found again?"
translations.idiomatic: Where will we find their like again?"

sentences.zh: 因嘆息久之。

translations.literal: and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 廷璐子若需，進士，官侍講。

translations.literal: Tinglu's son Ruoxu was a jinshi and served as Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglu's son Ruoxu was a jinshi and Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 若需子曾敞，進士，官少詹事。

translations.literal: Ruoxu's son Zengchang was a jinshi and served as Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu's son Zengchang was a jinshi and Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 自英後，以科第世其家，四世皆為講官。

translations.literal: After Ying, the family inherited office through the examinations for four generations, all serving as lecturers.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Ying the family held office through examinations for four generations, all as court lecturers.

sentences.zh: 陳廷敬，初名敬，字子端，山西澤州人。

translations.literal: Chen Tingjing, original name Jing, style name Ziduan, was a native of Zezhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tingjing, originally named Jing, courtesy name Ziduan, came from Zezhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 15 jinshi, he entered the Hanlin as a Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 是科館選，又有順天通州陳敬，上為加「廷」字以別之。

translations.literal: In that year's Hanlin selection there was also Chen Jing of Tongzhou in Shuntian; the Emperor added the character "Ting" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: That year another Chen Jing of Tongzhou was selected; the Emperor added "Ting" to his name to distinguish them.

sentences.zh: 十八年，充會試同考官，尋授秘書院檢討。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he served as associate examiner of the metropolitan examination and soon was appointed Reviser of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was associate metropolitan examiner, then Secretariat Reviser.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，假歸，四年，補原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he took leave to return home; in the fourth year he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 he went home on leave; in year 4 he resumed office.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林院侍講學士，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Hanlin Lecturer and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin Lecturer and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢內閣學士，兼禮部侍郎，充經筵講官，改翰林院掌院學士，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician and concurrently Vice Minister of Rites, appointed Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, made Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and instructed Hanlin Bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he became Grand Secretariat Academician and Vice Minister of Rites, Classics Colloquium lecturer, Hanlin Chancellor, and tutor to bachelors.

sentences.zh: 與學士張英日直弘德殿，聖祖器之，與英及掌院學士喇沙裡同賜貂皮五十、表裡緞各二。

translations.literal: Together with Academician Zhang Ying he attended daily at the Hall of Manifest Virtue; the Kangxi Emperor valued them and together with Ying and Chancellor Lashali granted fifty sable pelts and two bolts of satin each inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Ying he attended daily at Hongde Hall; the Emperor valued them and with Chancellor Lashali gave each fifty sables and two bolts of satin.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命直南書房。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was ordered to enter the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he entered the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，遣官慰問，賜茶酒。

translations.literal: On his mother's death, officials were sent to console him and tea and wine were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, officers were sent to console him with tea and wine.

sentences.zh: 服除，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he ran the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 滇南平，更定朝會燕饗樂章，命廷敬撰擬，下所司肄習。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, court assembly and banquet music was revised; Tingjing was ordered to draft it and the relevant offices to practice.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan's pacification, court and banquet music was revised; Tingjing drafted the new scores for practice.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調吏部，兼管戶部錢法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was transferred to Personnel and concurrently supervised Revenue coinage policy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he moved to Personnel while overseeing Revenue coinage.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「自古鑄錢時輕時重，未有數十年而不改者。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "From antiquity coinage has been light at times and heavy at times; there has never been several decades without change.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Coinage has always varied in weight; decades pass without reform.

sentences.zh: 向日銀一兩易錢千，今僅得九百，其故在毀錢鬻銅。

translations.literal: Formerly one tael of silver exchanged for a thousand cash; now one obtains only nine hundred—the reason lies in destroying coins to sell copper.
translations.idiomatic: Once a tael bought a thousand cash; now only nine hundred—because people melt coins for copper.

sentences.zh: 順治十年因錢賤壅滯，改舊重一錢者為一錢二分五釐，十七年又增為一錢四分，所以杜私鑄也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi, because coins were cheap and stagnant, the old weight of one qian was changed to one qian two fen five li; in the seventeenth year it was again increased to one qian four fen, in order to stop private casting.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 10 raised coin weight from one to one-and-a-quarter qian; Shunzhi 17 to one-and-four qian—to stop private minting.

sentences.zh: 今私鑄自如，應改重為輕，則毀錢不禁自絕。

translations.literal: Now private casting continues as before; the weight should be changed from heavy to light, and destroying coins will stop of itself without prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Private minting persists; he urged lightening coins so melting would cease without bans.

sentences.zh: 產銅之地，宜停收稅，聽民開採，則銅日多，錢價益平。」

translations.literal: In copper-producing regions, tax collection should be stopped and the people allowed to mine, so copper will daily increase and the price of money will be more level."
translations.idiomatic: In copper districts he urged ending mining taxes so supply would grow and prices stabilize."

sentences.zh: 疏下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the ministries for discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries adopted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「古者衣冠、輿馬、服飾、器用，賤不得逾貴，小不得加大。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In antiquity in dress, carriages, clothing, and utensils the low might not exceed the high, nor the small surpass the great.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Anciently dress, carriages, and utensils kept inferiors below superiors.

sentences.zh: 今等威未辨，奢侈未除，機絲所織，花草蟲魚，時新時異，轉相慕效。

translations.literal: Now ranks are not distinguished and extravagance is not removed; what machine-spun silk weaves—flowers, grasses, insects, fish—changes with fashion and people imitate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and frugality collapsed; novelty in silk patterns spread by imitation.

sentences.zh: 由是富者黷貨無已，貧者恥其不如，冒利觸禁，其始由於不儉，其繼至於不廉。

translations.literal: Hence the rich amass goods without end and the poor are shamed not to match them; they risk profit and break prohibitions—the start from lack of thrift, the sequel to lack of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The rich spent endlessly; the poor imitated them into corruption, beginning in extravagance and ending in graft.

sentences.zh: 請敕廷臣嚴申定制，以挽頹風。」

translations.literal: Request an edict that court ministers strictly enforce established regulations to reverse the declining trend."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to enforce sumptuary law and reverse decline."

sentences.zh: 又言：「方今要務，首在督撫得人。

translations.literal: He also said: "At present the foremost task is to obtain worthy governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The urgent need is worthy provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 為督撫者，不以利欲動其心，然後能正身以董吏。

translations.literal: As governors-general and governors, if profit and desire do not move their hearts, then they can correct themselves and oversee officials.
translations.idiomatic: Governors unmoved by greed can correct themselves and supervise subordinates.

sentences.zh: 吏不以曲事上官為心，然後能加意於民；

translations.literal: If officials do not take currying favor with superiors as their aim, then they can devote attention to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Officials who need not flatter superiors can care for the people;

sentences.zh: 民可徐得其養，養立而後教行。

translations.literal: the people may gradually obtain nurture; once nurture is established, then teaching can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: the people can be nourished, and once nourished, instructed.

sentences.zh: 宜飭督撫凡保薦州縣吏，必具列無加派火耗、無黷貨詞訟、無朘削富民。

translations.literal: Governors-general and governors should be ordered that whenever they recommend prefectural and county officials, they must list in full no added meltage, no corrupt taking in lawsuits, no squeezing of wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that recommendations list freedom from meltage surcharges, bribery, and extortion.

sentences.zh: 每月吉集眾講解聖諭，使知功令之重在此。

translations.literal: On auspicious days each month gather the people to explain the Sacred Edicts so they know where the weight of regulations lies.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly lectures on the Sacred Edicts should show where official duty lies.

sentences.zh: 而皇上考察督撫，則以潔己教吏，吏得一心養民教民為稱職，庶幾大法而小廉。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor examines governors-general and governors, let purity in self and teaching officials, and officials able with single mind to nurture and teach the people, be the standard of fitness—then perhaps great law and small integrity."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor should judge governors by personal integrity and officials' care for the people—then law and honesty may align."

sentences.zh: 又言：「水旱兇荒，堯、湯之世所不能盡無，惟備及於豫而周當其急，故民恃以無恐。

translations.literal: He also said: "Flood, drought, and famine—even in the age of Yao and Tang could not be entirely absent; only if preparation reaches beforehand and relief comes when urgent will the people rely on it without fear.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Even Yao and Tang knew flood and famine; timely stores and swift relief keep the people unafraid.

sentences.zh: 山東去年題報​​水災，戶部初議行令履勘，繼又行令分晰地畝高下，今年四月始行覆準蠲免。

translations.literal: Shandong last year reported flood disaster; Revenue at first proposed sending orders for on-site survey, then again orders to distinguish high and low fields by mu; only in the fourth month of this year was confirmation sent for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's flood report led Revenue to order surveys, then field classification—exemption was not confirmed until April.

sentences.zh: 如此其遲回者，所行之例則然耳。

translations.literal: Such delay comes simply from the regulations in force.
translations.idiomatic: Such delay followed routine regulations alone.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為被災分數既有冊結可據，即宜具覆豁免，上宣聖主勤民之意，下慰小民望澤之心，中不使吏胥緣為弊竇。」

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that since the percentage of disaster already has registers as evidence, exemption should be reported at once, above proclaiming the sage ruler's care for the people, below comforting the people's hope for grace, and in between not letting clerks make loopholes for abuse."
translations.idiomatic: Since disaster shares were registered, he urged immediate exemption—proclaiming imperial care, comforting the people, and blocking clerkly abuse."

sentences.zh: 疏並議行。

translations.literal: Both memorials were discussed and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 與學士徐乾學奏進鑑古輯覽，上嘉其有裨治化，命留覽。

translations.literal: Together with Academician Xu Qianxue he memorialized presenting the Mirror of Antiquity Compendium; the Emperor praised its benefit to governance and ordered it retained for reading.
translations.idiomatic: With Xu Qianxue he presented the Mirror of Antiquity Compendium; the Emperor praised its value and kept it for study.

sentences.zh: 時修輯三朝聖訓、政治典訓、方略、一統志、明史，廷敬並充總裁官。

translations.literal: At the time the Sacred Instructions of Three Reigns, Political Institutions, Strategic Accounts, Comprehensive Gazetteer, and History of Ming were being compiled; Tingjing served as chief compiler for all.
translations.idiomatic: He headed compilations of the Three Reigns' Sacred Instructions, Political Institutions, strategic accounts, Gazetteer, and Ming History.

sentences.zh: 累調戶、吏二部。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Revenue and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Revenue and Personnel in turn.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，法司逮問湖廣巡撫張汧，汧曾齎銀赴京行賄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the judiciary arrested and questioned Huguang Governor Zhang Qian; Qian had once carried silver to the capital to offer bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 Governor Zhang Qian of Huguang was arrested for bringing silver to Beijing to bribe officials.

sentences.zh: 獄急，語涉廷敬及尚書徐乾學、詹事高士奇，上置勿問。

translations.literal: The case was urgent and words touched Tingjing and Minister Xu Qianxue and Junior Tutor Gao Shiqi; the Emperor set it aside and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated Tingjing, Xu Qianxue, and Gao Shiqi; the Emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 廷敬乃以父老，疏乞歸養，詔許解任，仍管修書事。

translations.literal: Tingjing then, because his father was old, memorialized begging to return home to support him; an edict permitted him to leave office but still to supervise book compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Citing an aged father, he sought leave to nurse him; the court released him but kept him over book projects.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，起左都御史，遷工部尚書，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was restored as Left Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Minister of Works, then Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he returned as Left Censor-in-Chief, then Works, then Justice.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，授戶部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: On his father's death, when mourning ended he was appointed Minister of Revenue, then transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning he became Minister of Revenue, then Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，拜文淵閣大學士，兼吏部，仍直經筵。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuange and concurrently Minister of Personnel, still attending the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In year 42 he became Wenyuange Grand Secretary and Minister of Personnel, still at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，扈從南巡，召試士子，命閱卷。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he accompanied the southern tour, summoned candidates for examination, and was appointed examiner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 he followed the southern tour, tested scholars, and served as examiner.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，以疾乞休，允之。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, he begged leave on account of illness; it was granted.
