translations.idiomatic: In year 49 he retired for illness; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 會大學士張玉書卒，李光地病在告，召廷敬仍入閣視事。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Zhang Yushu died and Li Guangdi was ill on leave, Tingjing was summoned again to enter the Grand Council and handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yushu died and Li Guangdi was ill, Tingjing was recalled to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，卒，上深惜之，親制輓詩一章，命皇三子允祉奠茶酒；

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, he died; the Emperor deeply regretted it, composed an elegy in his own hand, and ordered the third imperial son Yin Zhi to offer tea and wine;
translations.idiomatic: In year 51 he died; the Emperor mourned, wrote an elegy, and ordered Prince Yin Zhi to offer sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 又命部院大臣會其喪，賜白金千，諡文貞。

translations.literal: also ordered ministers of the ministries and courts to attend his funeral and granted one thousand taels of silver; posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: ministers attended his funeral, he received a thousand taels, and the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 廷敬初以賜石榴子詩受知聖祖，後進所著詩集，上稱其清雅醇厚，賜詩題卷端。

translations.literal: Tingjing at first won the Kangxi Emperor's notice through a poem on bestowed pomegranate seeds; later he presented his collected poems and the Emperor praised them as elegant, pure, and mellow and bestowed a poem inscribed at the scroll's head.
translations.idiomatic: He first won favor with a poem on imperial pomegranates; his collected verse the Emperor called elegant and pure, and inscribed the scroll.

sentences.zh: 嘗召見問朝臣誰能詩者，以王士禎對，又​​舉汪琬應博學鴻儒，並以文學有名於時。

translations.literal: Once summoned and asked which court ministers could write poetry, he answered Wang Shizhen; he also recommended Wang Wan for the Erudite Learning examination—both were famous in letters of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Asked which officials wrote poetry, he named Wang Shizhen and recommended Wang Wan for the erudite examination—both famed literati.

sentences.zh: 上御門召九卿舉廉吏，諸臣各有所舉，語未竟，上特問廷敬，廷敬奏：「知縣陸隴其、邵嗣堯皆清官，雖治狀不同，其廉則一也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor at the gate summoned the Nine Ministers to recommend honest officials; each minister had his own nomination and words were not finished when the Emperor specially asked Tingjing; Tingjing memorialized: "Magistrates Lu Longqi and Shao Siyao are both clean officials; though their governing records differ, in integrity they are one."
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience for honest officials, each minister had his own nominations; before they finished, the Emperor specially asked Tingjing, who replied: "Magistrates Lu Longqi and Shao Siyao are both clean officials; though their governing records differ, their integrity is the same."

sentences.zh: 乃皆擢御史。

translations.literal: Both were then promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Both were promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 始廷敬嘗亟稱兩人，或謂曰：「兩人廉而剛，剛易折，且多怨，恐及公。」

translations.literal: At first Tingjing had often praised the two men; someone said to him: "The two are clean but stern; sternness is easily broken and brings many resentments—I fear it will reach you."
translations.idiomatic: He had long praised them; someone said to him: "Both men are incorrupt but stern; sternness is easily broken and breeds many resentments—I fear it may reach you."

sentences.zh: 廷敬曰：「果賢歟，雖折且怨，庸何傷？」

translations.literal: Tingjing said: "If they are truly worthy, though broken and resented, what harm?"
translations.idiomatic: Tingjing replied: "If they are truly worthy, what harm though they break and make enemies?"

sentences.zh: 溫達，費莫氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Wenda, of the Feimo clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Wenda of the Feimo clan was a Bordered Yellow Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式授都察院都事，遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: From clerk he was appointed Director of Affairs in the Censorate and transferred to Vice Director in Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: From clerk he became Censorate Director of Affairs, then Revenue Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，授陝西道御史。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi, he was appointed Censor of the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 he was Shaanxi Circuit Censor.

sentences.zh: 遷吏科給事中，兼管佐領。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section and concurrently managed an assistant command.
translations.idiomatic: He became Personnel Supervising Secretary and managed an assistant command.

sentences.zh: 授兵部督捕理事官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner for Pursuit Affairs in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was made War Ministry Commissioner for Pursuit Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，命溫達隨皇七子允祜、都統都爾瑪管鑲黃旗大營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan and ordered Wenda to follow the seventh imperial son Yin You and Commandery Commander Duerma in managing the Bordered Yellow Banner main camp.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35, on campaign against Galdan, Wenda followed Prince Yin You and Duerma managing the Bordered Yellow main camp.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he was promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 he became Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 he became Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十年，命赴山西、陝西察驗驛馬，還，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, he was ordered to go to Shanxi and Shaanxi to inspect relay horses; on returning he was appointed Deliberative Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he inspected relay horses in Shanxi and Shaanxi, then became Deliberative Minister.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督巴錫劾游擊高鑑讞獄不當，並論提督李芳述徇隱，芳述亦劾巴錫，命溫達往按，鑑罪應徒，巴錫左遷，芳述罰俸。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Ba Xi impeached Battalion Commander Gao Jian for improper judgment in a case and also charged Regional Commander Li Fangshu with shielding him; Fangshu also impeached Ba Xi; Wenda was ordered to investigate; Jian's crime warranted penal servitude, Ba Xi was demoted, Fangshu fined one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ba Xi and Commander Li Fangshu cross-impeached over a case; Wenda found Gao Jian guilty of penal servitude, demoted Ba Xi, and fined Fangshu.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，調吏部，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, he was transferred to Personnel and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 he moved to Personnel and became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，復命往貴州按威寧總兵孟大志侵餉，論罪如律。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he was again ordered to Guizhou to investigate Weining Regional Commander Meng Dazhi's embezzlement of pay; punishment followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 42 he investigated Meng Dazhi of Weining for embezzling military pay and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，遷工部尚書，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, he was transferred to Minister of Works and appointed Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 he became Minister of Works and Classics Colloquium lecturer.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，授文華殿大學士，纂修國史、政治典訓、平定朔漠方略、大清一統志、明史，並充總裁。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and compiled the National History, Political Institutions, Veritable Records of the Pacification of the Northern Deserts, Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Qing, and History of Ming, serving as chief compiler for all.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and served as chief compiler for the National History, Political Institutions and Instructions, the Veritable Records of the Pacification of the Northern Desert, the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Qing, and the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 五十年，命八旗及部院舉孝義，因諭曰：「孝為百行首。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, the Eight Banners and ministries and courts were ordered to recommend filial piety and righteousness; the Emperor thereupon said: "Filial piety is the head of the hundred conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In year 50 the court sought models of filial piety; the Emperor said: "Filial piety heads all virtues.

sentences.zh: 如大學士溫達，尚書穆和倫、富寧安之孝，不特眾所知，朕亦深知之也。」

translations.literal: Such as Grand Secretary Wenda and Ministers Mu Helun and Fu Ning'an—their filial piety is not only known to the multitude; I also know it deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wenda and Ministers Mu Helun and Fu Ning'an are known to all for filial piety, and I know it well."

sentences.zh: 御製詩以賜，复褒其孝友。

translations.literal: He composed a poem in his own hand and bestowed it, again praising his filial piety and brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor composed and bestowed a poem praising his filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，以老乞休，許致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, he begged retirement on account of age; retirement was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 53 he retired for age; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋諭溫達雖老，尚自康健，命仍任大學士。

translations.literal: Soon the Emperor said that though Wenda was old, he was still himself healthy and ordered him to continue as Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Emperor, finding him still healthy, ordered him to remain Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，卒，命皇子奠茶酒，賜祭葬，諡文簡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, he died; princes were ordered to offer tea and wine, funeral sacrifices were bestowed, posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 54 he died; princes sacrificed, funeral honors were granted, and he received the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 穆和倫，喜塔臘氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Mu Helun, of the Xitala clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Blue.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helun of the Xitala clan was a Bordered Blue Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 自兵部筆帖式四遷為御史，又三遷為內閣學士。

translations.literal: From War Ministry clerk through four promotions he became Censor, and through three more promotions Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: From War Ministry clerk he rose through four steps to Censor and three more to Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 命往山東察賑，自泰安至郯城。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Shandong to inspect famine relief from Tai'an to Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected famine relief in Shandong from Tai'an to Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十三年，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Kangxi, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 43 he became Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 48 he became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, he was transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 49 he moved to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上稱穆和倫孝，其母年已九十，御書「北堂眉壽」榜賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Mu Helun's filial piety; his mother was already ninety, and the Emperor wrote in his own hand the plaque "North Hall Eyebrow Longevity" and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised Mu Helun's filial piety; his mother was ninety, and he gave her the plaque "North Hall Eyebrow Longevity."

sentences.zh: 兩江總督噶禮與巡撫張伯行互劾，命穆和倫往按，右噶禮，上責其是非顛倒，終直伯行。

translations.literal: The Governors-General of the Two Jiangs Gali and Governor Zhang Boxing impeached each other; Mu Helun was ordered to investigate and favored Gali; the Emperor rebuked him for reversing right and wrong and ultimately upheld Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-General Gali and Governor Zhang Boxing cross-impeached; Mu Helun favored Gali; the Emperor rebuked his judgment and upheld Boxing.

sentences.zh: 尋以老病乞休，復起授戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he begged leave on account of age and illness; he was again restored and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired for age and illness, then was restored as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 坐事當左遷。

translations.literal: For an offense he was due to be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He was slated for demotion over an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 蕭永藻，漢軍鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yongzao was a Bannerman of the Bordered White.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yongzao was a Bordered White Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 父養元，管佐領。

translations.literal: His father Yangyuan managed an assistant command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yangyuan held an assistant command.

sentences.zh: 永藻自廕生補刑部筆帖式。

translations.literal: Yongzao from hereditary clerk filled a clerkship in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: As a hereditary clerk he entered the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，授內閣中書，遷禮部員外郎，襲佐領。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi, he was appointed Secretariat Secretary and transferred to Vice Director in Rites, inheriting the assistant command.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 he became Secretariat Secretary, then Rites Vice Director, inheriting his father's command.

sentences.zh: 遷郎中，監湖口稅務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director and supervised the Hukou tax office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director and supervised Hukou customs.

sentences.zh: 授御史，再遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor and again transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Censor, then Intendant of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he was promoted to Governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 he became Governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「錢多價賤，每千市價三錢二三分，兵領一兩之餉，不及數錢之用。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Cash is plentiful and the price low; each thousand sells for three fen two or three li; soldiers receiving one tael of pay obtain less than a few qian in use.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Cash is cheap at three fen odd per thousand; a soldier's tael buys almost nothing.

sentences.zh: 民亦因錢賤，貨物難行。

translations.literal: The people also because cash is cheap find goods hard to move.
translations.idiomatic: Cheap cash also paralyzed trade for civilians.

sentences.zh: 請暫停鼓鑄。」

translations.literal: Request a temporary halt to minting."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to suspend minting temporarily."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「開山發礦，多人群聚，良莠淆雜，臣通飭嚴禁。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Opening mountains and issuing mining permits draws many people together, good and bad mixed; your servant has ordered strict prohibition throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Opening mountains for mining draws crowds together, mixing honest folk with the lawless; I have strictly forbidden this throughout.

sentences.zh: 近有長寧匪徒集眾私採，知縣尤鵬翔請飭部議處。」

translations.literal: Recently in Changning bandits gathered to mine privately; Magistrate You Pengxiang requested orders to the ministry for disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Recently Changning bandits gathered to mine privately; Magistrate You Pengxiang asked the ministry for disposition."

sentences.zh: 鵬翔坐奪官。

translations.literal: Pengxiang was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: You Pengxiang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，給事中湯右曾劾永藻與總督石琳於黎人爭鬥事，遲至一載始行具題；

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Supervising Secretary Tang Youzeng impeached Yongzao and Governor-General Shi Lin for a Li people fight, delaying a full year before reporting;
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 Tang Youzeng impeached Yongzao and Governor Shi Lin for delaying a year before reporting a Li conflict;

sentences.zh: 縱屬吏朘民，民困而為盜，海則電白、陽江，山則英德、翁源，橫行劫掠。

translations.literal: indulging subordinate officials in squeezing the people—the people were distressed and became bandits; on the sea at Dianbai and Yangjiang, in the mountains at Yingde and Wengyuan, they rampaged in robbery.
translations.idiomatic: his subordinates extorted the people until hardship drove them into banditry: along the coast at Dianbai and Yangjiang, and in the hills at Yingde and Wengyuan, they ranged about plundering.

sentences.zh: 上命與廣西巡撫彭鵬互調，入覲，上諭當命效鵬所行，並誡薦舉當擇清廉。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered mutual transfer with Guangxi Governor Peng Peng; on entering audience the Emperor instructed that he should be ordered to emulate what Peng did, and also warned that recommendations must select the clean and honest.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor swapped him with Peng Peng of Guangxi and told him to emulate Peng's integrity in recommendations.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 45 he became Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督石文晟劾容美土司田舜年不法，命左都御史梅鋗、內閣學士二格往讞，與文晟異議；

translations.literal: Huguang Governor-General Shi Wencheng impeached Rongmei native chieftain Tian Shunnian for lawlessness; Left Censor-in-Chief Mei Qiong and Grand Secretariat Academician Erge were ordered to judge the case and differed from Wencheng;
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shi Wencheng accused Tian Shunnian of Rongmei; Mei Qiong and Erge disagreed with him;

sentences.zh: 復命永藻與大學士席哈納、侍郎張廷樞覆讞，還奏舜年已死，無諸僭越狀。

translations.literal: Yongzao was again ordered with Grand Secretary Xi Hana and Vice Minister Zhang Tingshu to re-judge; on returning they memorialized that Shunnian was already dead and there were no acts of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzao with Xi Hana and Zhang Tingshu retried the case and found Tian Shunnian dead without usurpation.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，擢左都御史，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 46 he became Left Censor-in-Chief, then Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，湖南巡撫趙申喬與提督俞益謨交惡互劾，命永藻偕副都御史王度昭往按，得益謨違例缺兵額狀，申喬事事苛求，非大臣體，並擬奪官，上罷益謨，留申喬。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, Hunan Governor Zhao Shenqiao and Regional Commander Yu Yimo hated each other and mutually impeached; Yongzao was ordered together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Duzhao to investigate; Yimo's violation in leaving troop quotas unfilled was obtained; Shenqiao was harsh in every matter, not in the manner of a great minister—both were proposed for stripping of office; the Emperor dismissed Yimo and retained Shenqiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year, Hunan governor Zhao Shenqiao and regional commander Yu Yimo became hostile and impeached one another. Yongzao was ordered to investigate together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Duzhao; they found that Yu Yimo had violated regulations by leaving troop quotas unfilled, while Zhao Shenqiao was exacting in every matter and lacked the bearing of a senior minister. Both were proposed for dismissal, but the Emperor dismissed Yu Yimo and retained Zhao Shenqiao.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，調吏部，旋授文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, he was transferred to Personnel; soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 49 he moved to Personnel, then became Wenhua Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, he was listed among Deliberative Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 56 he joined the Deliberative Council.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，加太子太傅，命駐馬蘭峪守護景陵。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and ordered to garrison Malanyu to guard the Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzheng's accession he was made Grand Tutor and stationed at Malanyu to guard the Jing tomb.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，宗人府奏護陵宗室廣善越分請安，永藻不先阻，當奪官，上責永藻自恃其有操守，驕矜偏執，惟知阿諛允，長其傲慢狂肆之罪，如議奪官，仍命護陵自效。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, the Imperial Clan Court reported that clansman Guangshan guarding the mausoleum overstepped rank in requesting audience; Yongzao did not stop it first and should be stripped of office; the Emperor rebuked Yongzao for relying on his own integrity, proud and obstinate, knowing only to flatter and assent, lengthening arrogant and reckless offenses; as proposed he was stripped of office but still ordered to guard the mausoleum to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 he failed to stop a clansman's breach at the tomb; stripped of office for pride and flattery, he was kept on to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he died at age eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 嵩祝，赫舍里氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Song Zhu, of the Hesheli clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered White.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhu of the Hesheli clan was a Bordered White Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 父岱袞，事太宗，協管佐領。

translations.literal: His father Daigun served Taizong and jointly managed an assistant command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daigun served Taizong and held an assistant command.

sentences.zh: 兄來袞，自侍衛累遷至內三院學士，授世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: His elder brother Laigun rose in succession from guard to Academician of the Three Inner Courts and received the hereditary post of Batulabulehafan.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Laigun rose from guard to Inner Court Academician with a hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 嵩祝襲職，康熙九年，管佐領。

translations.literal: Song Zhu inherited the post; in the ninth year of Kangxi he managed an assistant command.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhu inherited the post and in Kangxi 9 managed an assistant command.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷護軍參領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was transferred to Deputy Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he became Guard Deputy Commander.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, he was promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33 he became Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，盛京旱，命與侍郎珠都納偕往，發海運米萬石散貧民，萬石平糶。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Shenyang suffered drought; he was ordered together with Vice Minister Zhuduna to go there, dispatch ten thousand shi of sea-transport grain to the poor, and sell ten thousand shi at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34 Shenyang drought sent him with Zhuduna to distribute ten thousand shi free and sell ten thousand shi at fair price.

sentences.zh: 還京，命复偕珠都納往開原等散米。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, he was ordered again together with Zhuduna to go to Kaiyuan and other places to distribute grain.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing he was sent again with Zhuduna to distribute grain at Kaiyuan and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「將軍等請散米，但言兵不言民。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Generals and others request to distribute grain but speak only of soldiers, not civilians.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Generals ask to feed troops but forget civilians.

sentences.zh: 此皆朕赤子，當一併給與，月與米一斗五升，至來歲四月。」

translations.literal: These are all My children—they should be given together, one dou five sheng of rice per month until the fourth month of next year."
translations.idiomatic: They are all My children—give soldiers and civilians alike one dou five sheng monthly until next April."

sentences.zh: 嵩祝等散米如上指，事畢還京師。

translations.literal: Song Zhu and the others distributed grain as directed; when the task was finished they returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhu distributed grain as ordered and returned.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，嵩祝管正黃旗行營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; Song Zhu managed the Bordered Yellow Banner field camp.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35, on campaign against Galdan, he managed the Bordered Yellow field camp.

sentences.zh: 師還，命統後隊緩行，待西路章奏。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was ordered to command the rear column to march slowly and await memorials from the western route.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he led the rear column slowly to await western dispatches.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎，改護軍統領。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War and made Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of War and Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，复扈上出塞駐寧夏，命昭武將軍喀斯喀等窮追噶爾丹，嵩祝參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he again accompanied the Emperor beyond the passes to garrison at Ningxia; the Emperor ordered General Zhaowu Kasika and others to pursue Galdan to the end; Song Zhu assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 he followed the Emperor to Ningxia and assisted Kasika's pursuit of Galdan.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹竄死，師至摩該圖，引還。

translations.literal: Galdan fled and died; when the army reached Moyaitu it turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan died in flight; the army turned back at Moyaitu.

sentences.zh: 四十年，遷正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, he was transferred to Commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he commanded the Bordered Yellow Chinese Brigade.

sentences.zh: 廣東官兵剿連州瑤失利，命嵩祝偕副都統達爾佔、侍郎傅繼祖往會總督石琳，調廣西、湖南兵進剿，即授廣州將軍。

translations.literal: Guangdong troops suppressing Yao in Lianzhou suffered defeat; Song Zhu was ordered together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Da'erzhan and Vice Minister Fu Jizu to join Governor-General Shi Lin, transfer Guangxi and Hunan troops for the campaign, and was at once appointed General of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangdong troops failed against Lianzhou Yao, Song Zhu joined Shi Lin, brought Guangxi and Hunan forces, and became Guangzhou General.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上諭以相機招撫。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, the Emperor instructed him to win over and pacify as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, the Emperor told him to pacify where possible.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，師次連州，檄三省官兵分佈要隘。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, the army halted at Lianzhou and issued proclamations to the three provinces' troops to deploy at key passes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 at Lianzhou he deployed troops of three provinces at key passes.

sentences.zh: 瑤人薙發請降，執戕官兵者九人誅之。

translations.literal: The Yao shaved their heads and requested surrender; nine who had killed officials were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao surrendered; nine who had killed officials were executed.

sentences.zh: 師引還，調正紅旗。

translations.literal: The army turned back; he was transferred to the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew; he was moved to the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，署奉天將軍。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he served as acting General of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 48 he acted as Fengtian General.

sentences.zh: 海盜舟泊雙島，挾火器出掠，遣兵擊殺三十馀人，得其舟一。

translations.literal: Pirate boats moored at Shuangdao, came out with firearms to plunder; he sent troops who killed more than thirty and captured one boat.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates at Shuangdao were attacked; over thirty were killed and one boat taken.

sentences.zh: 疏請山東水師兼巡奉天屬金州鐵山，又請選盛京滿洲兵千人習鳥槍，設火器營，皆從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Shandong naval forces also patrol Jinzho and Tieshan under Fengtian, and also requested selecting one thousand Shenyang Manchu troops to practice muskets and establish a firearms camp—both were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Shandong naval patrols to cover Fengtian waters and formed a thousand-man musket corps in Shenyang—both approved.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，授文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 51 he became Wenhua Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，上幸熱河，嵩祝從。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, the Emperor toured Rehe and Song Zhu followed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 55 he followed the Emperor to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 久不雨，上憂旱甚，遣嵩祝還京師，察諸大臣祈雨不躬至者劾奏。

translations.literal: For a long time there was no rain; the Emperor was deeply worried about drought and dispatched Song Zhu back to the capital to investigate and memorialize ministers who prayed for rain without attending in person.
translations.idiomatic: During drought the Emperor sent him to Beijing to impeach ministers who prayed for rain without attending.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，加太子太傅，修聖祖實錄及玉牒，並充總裁。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, compiled the Veritable Records and Imperial Genealogy of the Kangxi Emperor, and served as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzheng's accession he became Grand Tutor and chief compiler of Kangxi's Veritable Records and genealogy.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，奉天將軍噶爾弼奏貝子蘇努為將軍時，借放庫銀三萬馀，嵩祝坐徇隱，奪官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Fengtian General Ga'erbi memorialized that when Prince Sunu was general he lent out more than thirty thousand taels from the treasury; Song Zhu was punished for shielding him and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 he was dismissed for shielding Prince Sunu's lending of treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he died at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 王頊齡，字顓士，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Wang Xuling, style name Zhuan Shi, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuling, courtesy name Zhuan Shi, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父廣心，字農山。

translations.literal: His father Guangxin, style name Nongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangxin used the courtesy name Nongshan.

sentences.zh: 有文名。

translations.literal: He had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed literary renown.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，官御史，巡視京、通二倉，釐剔漕弊，奸猾屏跡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi, served as Censor, inspected the Beijing and Tongzhou granaries, cleaned up transport abuses, and the cunning vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 6 jinshi and censor, he inspected Beijing and Tongzhou granaries, ended transport abuses, and drove off grafters.

sentences.zh: 頊齡，康熙十五年進士，授太常寺博士。

translations.literal: Xuling, in the fifteenth year of Kangxi became a jinshi and was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuling passed as jinshi in Kangxi 15 and became Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十八年，舉博學鴻儒，召試一等，授編修，纂修明史，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was recommended for the Erudite Learning examination, summoned for testing and placed first class, appointed Compiler, compiled the History of Ming, and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he topped the erudite examination, became Compiler, worked on the Ming History, and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 二十一年上元節，聖祖禦乾清宮賜廷臣宴，仿柏梁體賦詩，頊齡與焉。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival of the twenty-first year, the Kangxi Emperor at the Palace of Heavenly Purity gave a banquet to court ministers and composed poetry in the style of the Cypress Beam; Xuling was among them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kangxi 21 Lantern Festival the Emperor feasted ministers at Qianqing and composed Cypress Beam verse; Xuling was present.

sentences.zh: 遷侍講，督四川學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lecturer and supervised Sichuan education.
translations.idiomatic: He became Lecturer and Sichuan Educational Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Senior Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，左都御史郭琇疏劾少詹事高士奇與頊齡弟鴻緒植黨營私，並詆頊齡與士奇結婚媾，交關為奸利。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu memorialized impeaching Junior Tutor Gao Shiqi and Xuling's younger brother Hongxu for forming factions for private gain, and also slandered Xuling for marrying his daughter to Shiqi and colluding for corrupt profit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 Guo Xiu impeached Gao Shiqi and Xuling's brother Hongxu for faction and accused Xuling of marrying into Shiqi's family for profit.

sentences.zh: 頊齡、士奇、鴻緒並休致，尋命頊齡留任如故。

translations.literal: Xuling, Shiqi, and Hongxu were all ordered to retire; soon Xuling was ordered to remain in his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xuling, Shiqi, and Hongxu were told to retire; Xuling was soon kept in office.

sentences.zh: 轉侍讀學士，以父憂歸，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting; on his father's death he returned home; when mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He became Reader-in-Waiting, mourned his father, then resumed office.

sentences.zh: 累擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，上南巡，幸頊齡所居秀甲園，賜御書榜。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, on the southern tour the Emperor visited Xuling's dwelling the Xiujia Garden and bestowed an imperial plaque.
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 the southern tour visited his Xiujia Garden and bestowed an imperial plaque.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上南巡閱河，再幸其第。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, on the southern tour to inspect the river, the Emperor again visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In year 46, inspecting rivers on tour, the Emperor visited again.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Personnel and appointed Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Personnel and lectured at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 擢工部尚書，典會試。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works and presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Works and metropolitan examiner.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，拜武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year 55 he became Wuying Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔開恩榜，頊齡重與鹿鳴宴，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, an edict opened a grace examination list; Xuling again attended the Deer-Ming banquet and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he again attended the grace-examination banquet and was made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 以老，累疏乞休，上以頊齡先朝舊臣，勤勞歲久，諳習典章，輒與慰留。

translations.literal: On account of age he repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; because Xuling was an old minister of the previous reign, diligent over many years and versed in regulations, the Emperor repeatedly comforted him and urged him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Old and repeatedly seeking retirement, he was kept for long service and mastery of regulations.

sentences.zh: 三年，痰作，命御醫治疾，賜參餌。

translations.literal: In the third year, phlegm seized him; the Emperor ordered imperial physicians to treat the illness and bestowed ginseng medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 illness seized him; imperial physicians and ginseng were sent.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十四，上為輟朝一日，令朝臣出其門下者素服持喪、各部院漢官會祭，贈太傅，諡文恭。

translations.literal: Soon he died at age eighty-four; the Emperor suspended court one day, ordered court ministers who had been his students to wear plain dress and observe mourning, Han officials of the ministries and courts to join in sacrifice, posthumously made Grand Tutor, posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-four; the court mourned a day, students wore mourning, ministers sacrificed, and he received the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 弟九齡，字子武，進士，授編修，官至左都御史；

translations.literal: His younger brother Jiuling, style name Ziwu, was a jinshi, appointed Compiler, and rose to Left Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jiuling, courtesy name Ziwu, was a jinshi, Compiler, and Left Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 鴻緒，自有傳。

translations.literal: Hongxu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongxu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：玉書等遭際承平，致位宰相。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Yushu and the others met with peaceful times and reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator notes: Zhang Yushu and his peers rose in peaceful times to the premiership.

sentences.zh: 或以文學進，或以功能著，或以節操用，皆循循乎矩度。

translations.literal: Some advanced through literature, some were noted for ability, some were employed for integrity—all followed regulations step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Some rose by letters, some by competence, some by integrity—all kept within measure.

sentences.zh: 即朝旨所褒許，於玉書則曰「小心」，於天馥則曰「勤慎」，英曰「忠純」，琠曰「寬厚」，廷敬曰「清勤」，溫達「孝」，永藻「廉」，嵩祝「老成」，頊齡「安靜」。

translations.literal: Even the court's praise followed this: of Yushu it was said "careful," of Tianfu "diligent and cautious," of Ying "loyal and pure," of Tian "generous and mild," of Tingjing "clean and diligent," of Wenda "filial," of Yongzao "incorrupt," of Song Zhu "seasoned," of Xuling "quiet."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial praise matched each man: of Yushu it was said "careful," of Tianfu "diligent and cautious," of Ying "loyal and pure," of Tian "generous and mild," of Tingjing "clean and diligent," of Wenda "filial," of Yongzao "incorrupt," of Song Zhu "seasoned," of Xuling "quiet."

sentences.zh: 諸臣之行詣顯，世運之敦龐亦可見矣。

translations.literal: The conduct and attainments of these ministers were manifest—the solid prosperity of the age may also be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Their visible virtues reflect an age of solid prosperity.
